You have three seasons of ball-by-ball history in `league/` and a list of\n6\tfixtures for the coming season with the announced line-ups. For every fixture, give the probability that the home side wins.\n7\t\n8\tYou deliver a program. It is run on this league and on other leagues of the same kind that you have not seen, so it has to learn\n9\teverything it needs from the league folder it is given.\n10\t\n11\t    python solution/forecast.py --league <folder> --out <file.csv>\n12\t\n13\tThe output file has two columns, `fixture` and `p_home`, with one row per fixture in `<folder>/fixtures.csv`.\n14\t\n15\t## How a forecast is graded\n16\t\n17\tThe league is simulated, so the [REDACTED] probability that the home side wins each fixture is known exactly. Your forecast is graded against\n18\tthat number. No match is played and no result is used, so luck has no part in the grade.\n19\t\n20\tFor a fixture with [REDACTED] probability `p` and forecast `q`, the penalty is `p*ln(p/q) + (1-p)*ln((1-p)/(1-q))`. It is zero when `q = p` and\n21\tgrows quickly when a forecast is confident and wrong. Forecasts are clipped to [0.002, 0.998]. Your regret on a league is the\n22\taverage penalty over its fixtures.\n23\t\n24\tYour regret is compared with that of a reference forecaster. The reference uses only the files you have, the engine you have, and standard\n25\tstatistical practice. It plays each fixture 4,000 times. Your program is run on this league and on seven leagues you have not seen. You pass\n26\tif your regret, summed over all eight leagues, is at most 10 percent above the reference's sum, and the same holds for the seven\n27\tunseen leagues on their own. Simulation noise in your own forecasts counts against you, so play each fixture enough times.\n28\t\n29\tFor orientation, summed over leagues like these a coin flip (0.5 everywhere) has a little under twice the reference's regret. On a single\n30\tleague anything can happen. Some leagues have little to predict, and there the reference itself can be close to the coin flip.\n31\t\n32\t## The files in a league folder\n33\t\n34\t| file | one row per | columns |\n35\t|---|---|---|\n36\t| `balls.csv` | legal ball | `season, match, innings, over, ball, batting_team, bowling_team, venue, batter, bowler, outcome, extra, position, wickets_before, runs_before, target` |\n37\t| `matches.csv` | match | `season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss_winner, batted_first, first_total, second_total, winner` |\n38\t| `lineups.csv` | player in a past match | `match, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n39\t| `players.csv` | player | `player, role, hand, bowling_style` |\n40\t| `venues.csv` | venue | `venue, home_team, pitch` |\n41\t| `fixtures.csv` | fixture to forecast | `fixture, season, home, away, venue` |\n42\t| `fixture_lineups.csv` | player in a fixture | `fixture, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n43\t\n44\t`outcome` is one of `W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6`. `extra` is 1 when the ball also produced one extra run. `position` is the batter's place in the\n45\torder, from 0. `target` is 0 in the first innings. `bowling_slot` is -1 for players who do not bowl. `engine/league_io.py` reads a folder\n46\tinto the objects the engine uses.\n47\t\n48\t## How a ball works (all of this is public)\n49\t\n50\t`engine/model.py` is the engine, and `engine/public.json` holds its public constants. They are the exact definition; this section\n51\tdescribes them in words.\n52\t\n53\tEvery legal ball has six possible outcomes. Their probabilities come from a sum of effects on the log scale:\n54\t\n55\t1. a profile for the over being bowled (`over_logits`), a shift for the batter's position (`position_vectors`);\n56\t2. the match situation: how many more wickets have fallen than is usual at that over (`wickets_vector`), and in the second innings a\n57\t   constant shift plus the chase pressure, which is the log of the required run rate over the usual rate from that over on, clipped to\n58\t   [-1, 1.2] (`second_innings_vector`, `pressure_vector`, `par_rate`);\n59\t3. the batter's **style** and **quality**, the bowler's **type** and **quality**, and the **conditions**, each a single number that moves\n60\t   the six outcomes along a fixed public direction (`directions`).\n61\t\n62\tOn top of the ball, with a fixed probability one extra run is added (`extras_per_ball`). Batters bat in line-up order. The strike changes\n63\ton an odd number of runs and at the end of each over. The five bowlers bowl in rotation, one over each in turn. An innings ends after 120\n64\tlegal balls, ten wickets, or when the target is reached. The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. A tied match is settled by\n65\ta coin flip.\n66\t\n67\t## What is hidden, and how it is built\n68\t\n69\t* **Batters.** Style does not change. Quality is a fixed talent plus a form component that drifts slowly over months and is pulled back\n70\t  toward zero. A batter's quality can differ a little against pace and against spin. Every player bats, so every player has these values.\n71\t* **Bowlers.** Type is related to the public bowling style and does not change. Quality is talent plus slowly drifting form.\n72\t* **Conditions.** A level for each venue; a league-wide level that moves from season to season and keeps moving; a pitch-on-the-day\n73\t  effect drawn afresh for every match and shared by both innings; dew at some venues, which helps the chase; a small general\n74\t  disadvantage for the side batting second; a lift for batters at their home ground; a personal liking of each batter for each venue;\n75\t  small league-wide effects of batting hand against bowling style and of pitch type on bowling style.\n76\t* There is **no** effect that belongs to one specific batter against one specific bowler.\n77\t* Between seasons about a quarter of the players change teams, and line-ups rotate heavily from match to match.\n78\t\n79\tThe fixtures are played at the start of the next season. Skills are as they stand at that moment, after one more off-season of drift.\n80\t\n81\t## Rules for your program\n82\t\n83\t* Everything it needs must be under `solution/`. The entry point is `solution/forecast.py`. It may import `engine`, which the grader\n84\t  supplies unchanged, and `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy` and the Python standard library. Do not change anything under `engine/`.\n85\t* It must give the same output every time it is run on the same folder. Fix your random seeds.\n86\t* It has 12 minutes per league on two CPU cores and must not use the network.\n87\t* The engine is yours to use in any way you like, including to test your own method on leagues you simulate yourself.\n88\t\n89\t## Source\n90\t\n91\tCalibration constants derived from data sourced from Cricsheet (cricsheet.org), licensed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License\n92\t(ODC-BY 1.0). You have three seasons of ball-by-ball history in `league/` and a list of\nfixtures for the coming season with the announced line-ups. For every fixture, give the probability that the home side wins.\n\nYou deliver a program. It is run on this league and on other leagues of the same kind that you have not seen, so it has to learn\neverything it needs from the league folder it is given.\n\n    python solution/forecast.py --league <folder> --out <file.csv>\n\nThe output file has two columns, `fixture` and `p_home`, with one row per fixture in `<folder>/fixtures.csv`.\n\n## How a forecast is graded\n\nThe league is simulated, so the [REDACTED] probability that the home side wins each fixture is known exactly. Your forecast is graded against\nthat number. No match is played and no result is used, so luck has no part in the grade.\n\nFor a fixture with [REDACTED] probability `p` and forecast `q`, the penalty is `p*ln(p/q) + (1-p)*ln((1-p)/(1-q))`. It is zero when `q = p` and\ngrows quickly when a forecast is confident and wrong. Forecasts are clipped to [0.002, 0.998]. Your regret on a league is the\naverage penalty over its fixtures.\n\nYour regret is compared with that of a reference forecaster. The reference uses only the files you have, the engine you have, and standard\nstatistical practice. It plays each fixture 4,000 times. Your program is run on this league and on seven leagues you have not seen. You pass\nif your regret, summed over all eight leagues, is at most 10 percent above the reference's sum, and the same holds for the seven\nunseen leagues on their own. Simulation noise in your own forecasts counts against you, so play each fixture enough times.\n\nFor orientation, summed over leagues like these a coin flip (0.5 everywhere) has a little under twice the reference's regret. On a single\nleague anything can happen. Some leagues have little to predict, and there the reference itself can be close to the coin flip.\n\n## The files in a league folder\n\n| file | one row per | columns |\n|---|---|---|\n| `balls.csv` | legal ball | `season, match, innings, over, ball, batting_team, bowling_team, venue, batter, bowler, outcome, extra, position, wickets_before, runs_before, target` |\n| `matches.csv` | match | `season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss_winner, batted_first, first_total, second_total, winner` |\n| `lineups.csv` | player in a past match | `match, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n| `players.csv` | player | `player, role, hand, bowling_style` |\n| `venues.csv` | venue | `venue, home_team, pitch` |\n| `fixtures.csv` | fixture to forecast | `fixture, season, home, away, venue` |\n| `fixture_lineups.csv` | player in a fixture | `fixture, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n\n`outcome` is one of `W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6`. `extra` is 1 when the ball also produced one extra run. `position` is the batter's place in the\norder, from 0. `target` is 0 in the first innings. `bowling_slot` is -1 for players who do not bowl. `engine/league_io.py` reads a folder\ninto the objects the engine uses.\n\n## How a ball works (all of this is public)\n\n`engine/model.py` is the engine, and `engine/public.json` holds its public constants. They are the exact definition; this section\ndescribes them in words.\n\nEvery legal ball has six possible outcomes. Their probabilities come from a sum of effects on the log scale:\n\n1. a profile for the over being bowled (`over_logits`), a shift for the batter's position (`position_vectors`);\n2. the match situation: how many more wickets have fallen than is usual at that over (`wickets_vector`), and in the second innings a\n   constant shift plus the chase pressure, which is the log of the required run rate over the usual rate from that over on, clipped to\n   [-1, 1.2] (`second_innings_vector`, `pressure_vector`, `par_rate`);\n3. the batter's **style** and **quality**, the bowler's **type** and **quality**, and the **conditions**, each a single number that moves\n   the six outcomes along a fixed public direction (`directions`).\n\nOn top of the ball, with a fixed probability one extra run is added (`extras_per_ball`). Batters bat in line-up order. The strike changes\non an odd number of runs and at the end of each over. The five bowlers bowl in rotation, one over each in turn. An innings ends after 120\nlegal balls, ten wickets, or when the target is reached. The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. A tied match is settled by\na coin flip.\n\n## What is hidden, and how it is built\n\n* **Batters.** Style does not change. Quality is a fixed talent plus a form component that drifts slowly over months and is pulled back\n  toward zero. A batter's quality can differ a little against pace and against spin. Every player bats, so every player has these values.\n* **Bowlers.** Type is related to the public bowling style and does not change. Quality is talent plus slowly drifting form.\n* **Conditions.** A level for each venue; a league-wide level that moves from season to season and keeps moving; a pitch-on-the-day\n  effect drawn afresh for every match and shared by both innings; dew at some venues, which helps the chase; a small general\n  disadvantage for the side batting second; a lift for batters at their home ground; a personal liking of each batter for each venue;\n  small league-wide effects of batting hand against bowling style and of pitch type on bowling style.\n* There is **no** effect that belongs to one specific batter against one specific bowler.\n* Between seasons about a quarter of the players change teams, and line-ups rotate heavily from match to match.\n\nThe fixtures are played at the start of the next season. Skills are as they stand at that moment, after one more off-season of drift.\n\n## Rules for your program\n\n* Everything it needs must be under `solution/`. also public\n22\t    home_team: np.ndarray\n23\t    pitch: np.ndarray # 0 neutral, 1 helps pace, 2 helps spin\n24\t\n25\t@dataclass\n26\tclass Fixture:\n27\t    # one match's line-ups: the eleven and the five bowlers for each side, plus where and when it is played\n28\t    match: int\n29\t    season: int\n30\t    home: int\n31\t    away: int\n32\t    venue: int\n33\t    home_xi: np.ndarray\n34\t    home_bowlers: np.ndarray\n35\t    away_xi: np.ndarray\n36\t    away_bowlers: np.ndarray\n37\t\n38\t@dataclass\n39\tclass History:\n40\t    # everything an AI agent is allowed to see about the past: every ball, every match, the players, the grounds, the line-ups\n41\t    balls: pd.DataFrame\n42\t    matches: pd.DataFrame\n43\t    players: PlayerTable\n44\t    venues: VenueTable\n45\t    played: list = field(default_factory = list) # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n46\t    seasons: int = 0\n47\t\n48\t@dataclass\n49\tclass BattingCard:\n50\t    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n82\t        \"\"\"\n83\t        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n84\t        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n85\t        cal = self.cal\n86\t        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n87\t        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n88\t\n89\t    @staticmethod\n90\t    def shares(z):\n91\t        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n92\t        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n93\t        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n94\t\n95\t# Innings Simulator\n96\tclass InningsSimulator:\n97\t    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. Every array below would have one entry per copy, so a ball is one vectorized step.\n98\t    def __init__(self, model):\n99\t        self.model = model\n100\t\n101\t    def play(self, batting, bowling, conditions, n, gen, target = None, log = None):\n102\t        \"\"\"\n103\t        Plays n copies of one innings and returns the n totals.\n104\t        `conditions` is a number of one value per copy.\n105\t        \"\"\"\n106\t        m, rows = self.model, np.arange(n)\n107\t        # who is on strike, who is at the other end, and who comes in next, as positions 0 to 10 in batting order\n108\t        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n109\t        # wickets lost, runs scored, and whether this copy's innings is still going\n110\t        wickets = np.zeros(n, int)\n111\t        runs = np.zeros(n, int)\n112\t        live = np.ones(n, bool)\n113\t        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n114\t        for ball in range(120):\n115\t            over = ball // 6\n116\t            # five bowlers rotate over by over; the [REDACTED] league has none\n        return 0.0                       # the [REDACTED] league has no effect tied to one specific batter-bowler pair\n\n    def shift(self, venue, chasing):\n        # the conditions shared by every ball of an innings: the ground's level, the season level, and in a chase the dew minus the wear\n        return self.venue_level[venue] + self.era + ((self.venue_dew[venue] - self.wear) if chasing else 0.0)\n\n\nclass MatchSimulator:\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.innings = InningsSimulator(model)\n\n    def win_probability(self, book, fixture, n, gen):\n        \"\"\"\n        P(home side wins). \n        The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. \n        A tie is settled by a coin flip.\n        \"\"\"\n        f = fixture\n        xi, five = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}, {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n        total = 0.0\n        # both orders of batting are played, each with weight one half, because the toss decides who chases\n        for first, second in ((f.home, f.away), (f.away, f.home)):\n            day = gen.normal(0.0, book.day_sd, n) if book.day_sd > 0 else np.zeros(n)       # the same pitch for both innings of a copy\n            set_ = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[first], first, five[second], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, False) + day, n, gen)\n            chase = self.innings.play(*book.cards(xi[second], second, five[first], f.venue), book.shift(f.venue, True) + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n            # the chasing side wins if it passes the total; a tie is worth half\n            second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n            total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second == f.home else 1 - second_wins)\n        return float(total)\n\n\nclass PublicConstants:\n    \"\"\"\n    The documented structure of a ball: \n        everything in the engine that is not a hidden skill or a hidden condition.\n    \"\"\"\n    # This is what ships to the agent as public.json: the profiles, the situation responses, the directions and the extras rate.\n    # The spreads, the venue spread and the real targets from calibration.json are deliberately not in it.\n    FIELDS = (\"over_logits\", \"position_vectors\", \"wickets_vector\", \"pressure_vector\", \"second_innings_vector\", \"typical_wickets\", \"par_rate\")\n\n    def __init__(self, raw):\n        for name in self.FIELDS:\n            setattr(self, name, np.array(raw[name]))\n        self.directions = {k: np.array(v) for k, v in raw[\"directions\"].items()}\n        self.extras_per_ball = raw[\"extras_per_ball\"]\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_calibration(cls, cal):\n        raw = {name: getattr(cal, name).tolist() for name in cls.FIELDS}\n        raw.update(directions={k: v.tolist() for k, v in cal.directions.items()}, extras_per_ball=cal.extras_per_ball)\n        return raw\n\n\ndef load_public_model(path=None):\n    # what the AI agent's copy of the engine does: build a BallModel from public.json beside it\n    raw = json.loads(Path(path or Path(__file__).with_name(\"public.json\")).read_text())\n    return BallModel(PublicConstants(raw))","numLines":233,"startLine":1,"totalLines":233}}}

wickets_before = balls.wickets_before.to_numpy()\n    runs_before = balls.runs_before.to_numpy()\n    target = balls.target.to_numpy()\n    ball_in_over = balls.ball.to_numpy()\n    innings =   D_T = D.T  # (6, 5)\n\n    offsets = {}\n    o = 0\n\n    def alloc(name, size):\n        nonlocal o\n        offsets[name] = (o, o + size)\n        o += size\n\n    alloc(\"style\", N_p)\n    alloc(\"quality\", N_p)\n    alloc(\"split\", N_p)\n    alloc(\"kind\", N_p)\n    alloc(\"bowl_quality\", N_p)\n    alloc(\"venue_level\", N_v)\n    alloc(\"venue_dew\", N_v)\n    alloc(\"affinity\", Every ball's 6-outcome distribution is a softmax of `z_public + F·D`, where `F = [bat_style, bat_quality, bowl_type, bowl_quality, conditions]` per ball and `D` stacks the five public direction vectors. Parameters fit:\n   - Per player: `style, quality, split, kind, bowl_quality`\n   - Per venue: `venue_level, venue_dew`, plus per-(player,venue) `affinity`\n   - Global: `wear, home_lift`, per-season `era`, per-match `day_effect`\n   - `type_table[hand, bowl_style]` and `pitch_table[bowl_style, pitch]`\n   \n   The full model is convex; solved with L-BFGS in ~110 iterations using analytic gradients via `np.bincount` scatters.\n3. **Build a `SkillBook`** with fitted values; `era ← era[last_season]` (best guess under a random walk), `day_sd ← std(day_effect_estimates)`.\n4. **Simulate 10,000 copies** per fixture via `MatchSimulator.win_probability` (which uses the [REDACTED] engine).\n\n**Verification**:\n- Deterministic (fixed `np.random.default_rng` seeds).\n- ~35s per league on this data (12-minute budget).\n- Zero-skill sanity: symmetric fixture gives `p_home ≈ 0.496`.\n- Forecast range (0.27–0.72) shows moderate confidence with mild home advantage, consistent with the observed 57% historical home-win rate."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2154,"cache_read_input_tokens":101441,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2154},"output_tokens":11,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c21ba0b1-8892-457a-89e2-aa99ba7319b8","uuid":"90e4ea8d-6875-4578-b521-8c6545610ef6","timestamp":"2026-09-24T02:29:18.771Z","request_id":"req_011CfMUb5om7MHq5UMH2UYDe"}
